scenes.title: Open Analytics and read the reporting scope
scenes.narration_exact: In Core, open the Records navigation and choose Analytics. The selected Executive summary tab gives the department's recorded summary. Start with From, To, Station slash group and Definition. This example displays August second through October thirty-first, with All station groups and All definitions selected. Read the Generated line and Records read count with those filters. The page says that dashboards are computed on demand over finalized Records, and that viewers see the Records they are authorized to open. Your account's access and the displayed reporting scope both matter when comparing results.

scenes.title: Read headline figures with the prior period
scenes.narration_exact: Scroll to Headline figures and read the prior-period dates before comparing values. Here, Records finalized is four, Personnel hours and Training hours are each zero point five, and Amendments is one. Incident reports, unit responses and the NERIS counts are zero in this fictional dataset. The values beneath the tiles show their comparison with the prior period. These are measures derived from the saved software records. They do not independently confirm physical attendance, service delivery or a department's real operational performance.

scenes.title: Distinguish lifecycle, queue and breakdown measures
scenes.narration_exact: Continue to Lifecycle, Queues and obligations, By month and By definition. Median hours to finalize is zero point one here, while several unavailable measures show a dash. A dash is not a measured zero. Open drafts shows one and Awaiting review shows zero. Those are current visible-queue counts, rather than the finalized-record count of a selected definition. The breakdown tables show four October records, split between two Training records and two community software-exercise records. Use the headings, counts, hours and shares together to understand what each panel is describing.

scenes.title: Select a definition before refreshing
scenes.narration_exact: Return to the filter row and select Training in Definition. Before you choose Filter, the earlier Generated line still says Records read, four. This separates a prepared field selection from refreshed dashboard output. Check the intended dates and group at the same time, then choose Filter to request the new result. Selecting a reporting filter changes the question you ask of the saved data; it does not edit, finalize or delete a record.

scenes.title: Keep record and transition scopes distinct
scenes.narration_exact: In this filtered result, Records finalized and Training hours are zero, while Amendments still shows one. For this department-administrator account, that amendment figure counts department transitions in the time window; it is not the finalized-record count of the selected group. The empty breakdown panels say No finalized Records in this window. Read the actual label and scope of each measure before using it to explain a change or assess a department's workload.

scenes.title: Read workload counts, hours and shares
scenes.narration_exact: Scroll to By month and By definition. October contains four records and zero point five hours. In the definition table, Training has two records, zero point five hours and a fifty-percent share. The community software-exercise definition also has two records and a fifty-percent share, but zero recorded hours. Equal record counts do not mean equal recorded duration. Read all three columns before deciding where more detail or a closer records review is needed.

scenes.title: Use a clear reporting question for your department
scenes.narration_exact: Start with a reporting question that matches your department's records. Community paramedicine and mental health teams can review outreach documentation, search-and-rescue teams can compare mission-support records, security companies can examine recorded service activity, and wildland or industrial response teams can review their own documented work. Fire and EMS departments can use the same filter and readback habits. Choose the intended window, definition and group, refresh the view, then investigate the underlying records before drawing conclusions from a count or hour total.
